messages.subject: oSCR.parfit() iteration limit error
messages.body_plain:
Has anyone run into the following error with oSCR.parfit(). It is thrown within a few minutes of the models starting up.

"Error in { : task 1 failed - "invalid iteration limit in nlm””

The call:
dens.mods <- oSCR.parfit( mods=mods.d,
                          scrFrame=ms.sf,
                          ssDF=ms.ssDF,
                          trimS=35E3,
                          ncores=6)

Best,
Clayton

messages.subject: Re: [oscr] oSCR.parfit() iteration limit error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Clay,

Not sure what’s happening there. Trouble with the parfit function is that there is lot happening n the fly in terms of function calls, despite its ultimate function being quite straightforward. Personally, I have started directly running models in parallel (i.e., just writing the few lines of code parfit needs to, just without all the generalization and automation). So, here is a short script that mirrors the parfit workflow, but at the end does the parallelization directly. Grey is just setting up the bear data, blue is what you want to focus on!

library(oSCR)

data(beardata)

#create the ‘time’ time varying covariate

beardata$tdf$sep <- '/'

beardata$tdf$rand1 <- rnorm(nrow(beardata$tdf))

beardata$tdf$rand2 <- rnorm(nrow(beardata$tdf))

#create scrframe

data <-data2oscr(edf=beardata$edf,

                 tdf=list(beardata$tdf),

                 sess.col=which(colnames(beardata$edf)%in%"Session"),

                 id.col=which(colnames(beardata$edf)%in%"ID"),

                 occ.col=which(colnames(beardata$edf)%in%"Occasion"),

                 trap.col=which(colnames(beardata$edf)%in%"trapID"),

                 sex.col=which(colnames(beardata$edf)%in%"Sex"),

                 sex.nacode="NA",

                 K=8,

                 tdf.sep = "/",

                 trapcov.names = c("rand1","rand2"),

                 ntraps=nrow(beardata$tdf))

bear.sf <-data$scrFrame

bear.ss <-make.ssDF(scrFrame = bear.sf, buffer = 2, res = 1)

(mods <- make.mods(density = c(~1),

                   detection = c(~1,~rand1,~rand2),

                   sigma = c(~1)))

library(foreach)

library(doParallel)

cl <- makeCluster(3)    #make the cluster

registerDoParallel(cl)  #register the cluster

out2 <- foreach(i=1:3,.packages = "oSCR") %dopar% {

  m <- list(mods[i,1][[1]], # ith model

            mods[i,2][[1]],

            mods[i,3][[1]],

            mods[i,4][[1]]) #this is a bit clumsy, but its morning here ☹

  out <- oSCR.fit(m, bear.sf,bear.ss, trimS=2)

  return(out)

}

stopCluster(cl)

Hope that helps. Actually, probably better from a #learnR perspective to be able to do this rather than rely on the wrapper 😊

Chris
